subject: Environment
description: Wildlife Protection Act, Project Tiger, IUCN, CITES

questions.stem: Project Tiger, launched by the Government of India to save the Indian tiger, began in:
questions.explanation: Project Tiger was launched on 1 April 1973 at Jim Corbett National Park (Uttarakhand) with 9 tiger reserves. The number has since grown to over 50. The tiger population, ~1,827 in the 1972 census, had fallen to ~1,411 in 2006 but rose to ~3,682 (± ~500) in the 2022 all-India tiger estimate — a major conservation success.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: The Wildlife Protection Act of India was enacted in:
questions.explanation: The Wildlife Protection Act, 1972 — created the legal framework for national parks, sanctuaries, and the Schedules of protected species (Schedule I carries the highest protection). Amended several times, most recently in 2022 to align with CITES Appendices. Other landmark green laws — Water Act 1974, Forest Conservation Act 1980, Environment (Protection) Act 1986, Biological Diversity Act 2002.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: The one-horned rhinoceros in India is found mainly in the state of:

options.option_text: Arunachal Pradesh
Assam
West Bengal
Manipur

questions.explanation: Assam's Kaziranga National Park (UNESCO WHS) hosts the world's largest population of the Indian one-horned rhinoceros (~2,600). Other rhino areas — Pobitora (Assam, highest density), Manas (Assam), Jaldapara and Gorumara (WB). Rhino poaching has fallen sharply after Assam police's crackdown and community engagement from ~2016. Project Rhino / Kaziranga Ranger Force is a state success story.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: The 'Asiatic lion', the last wild population of which is found in India, lives in the:

options.option_text: Bandipur forests
Gir forest of Gujarat
Ranthambore sanctuary
Corbett National Park

questions.explanation: Gir National Park in Junagadh district, Gujarat, is the only wild habitat of the Asiatic lion (Panthera leo persica). The 2020 census recorded around 674 lions. The population had dropped to ~20 in the early 20th century (the Nawab of Junagadh protected them). Plans to translocate some lions to Kuno (MP) have been debated but Kuno instead hosts cheetahs under Project Cheetah (2022).

questions.stem: The 'IUCN Red List' categorises species by their level of:

options.option_text: Commercial value
Extinction risk
Genetic similarity
Population size only

questions.explanation: IUCN Red List categorises species from 'Extinct' (EX) down through 'Extinct in the Wild' (EW), 'Critically Endangered' (CR), 'Endangered' (EN), 'Vulnerable' (VU), 'Near Threatened' (NT), 'Least Concern' (LC). Indian examples — Bengal tiger (EN), Asiatic lion (EN), Indian rhinoceros (VU), Great Indian bustard (CR), Gharial (CR). CITES separately regulates international trade in wildlife with three Appendices.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: The National Animal of India is the:

options.option_text: Lion
Bengal Tiger
Asian Elephant
Snow Leopard

questions.explanation: Bengal tiger (Panthera tigris tigris) — National Animal of India since 1973 (replacing the Asiatic lion). Peacock — National Bird (1963). Lotus — National Flower. Banyan — National Tree. Mango — National Fruit. Ganga Dolphin — National Aquatic Animal (2009). 'Roar' (bengal-tiger call) can carry ~2 km.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: The 'Olive Ridley' sea turtle, known for its mass nesting ('arribada') in India, is especially associated with:

options.option_text: Goa coast
Odisha coast
Gujarat coast (Gulf of Kachchh)
Lakshadweep coast

questions.explanation: Olive Ridley turtles arrive in massive synchronous nesting waves called arribadas at Gahirmatha (Bhitarkanika Marine Sanctuary) and Rushikulya in Odisha, every January-March. Around 4-5 lakh turtles nest every season — one of the world's largest aggregations. Tamil Nadu's Chennai coast sees small-scale olive-ridley nesting too, protected by groups like SSTCN. Gahirmatha, Rushikulya.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: Project Elephant, India's centrally sponsored scheme to protect wild elephants and their corridors, was launched in which year?

options.option_text: 1973, the same year Project Tiger was launched
1992, under the Ministry of Environment and Forests
1986, following the Environment Protection Act passage
2001, as part of the National Wildlife Action Plan

questions.explanation: Project Elephant was launched in 1992 by the Government of India to protect elephants, their habitats, and migration corridors. Option A is the most tempting distractor since candidates frequently conflate it with Project Tiger's 1973 launch, but the two are separate programmes two decades apart.

questions.stem: The Great Indian Bustard (Ardeotis nigriceps), listed as Critically Endangered by IUCN, is the official State Bird of which Indian state?

options.option_text: Gujarat, known for the Little Rann of Kutch wetlands
Rajasthan, where the Desert National Park is located
Andhra Pradesh, home to Rollapadu Wildlife Sanctuary
Madhya Pradesh, which hosts several notable bustard sightings

questions.explanation: The Great Indian Bustard is the State Bird of Rajasthan; Desert National Park in Jaisalmer is its primary remaining stronghold. Rollapadu in Andhra Pradesh (Option C) is a real GIB sanctuary and a strong distractor, but GIB is not Andhra Pradesh's state bird.

questions.stem: Which was India's first Biosphere Reserve, notified by the Government of India in 1986?

options.option_text: Sundarbans Biosphere Reserve, notified across West Bengal
Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, covering Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka
Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve along the Tamil Nadu coastline
Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve located in the Uttarakhand Himalaya

questions.explanation: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve was notified in 1986, making it India's first. It later became India's first UNESCO Man and Biosphere (MAB) Programme site. Gulf of Mannar and Sundarbans were both notified in 1989; Nanda Devi in 1988 — all post-Nilgiri.

questions.stem: Which of the following Indian wildlife species is currently classified as 'Vulnerable' — not 'Endangered' or 'Critically Endangered' — on the IUCN Red List?

options.option_text: Bengal Tiger (Panthera tigris tigris) — Endangered category
Gharial (Gavialis gangeticus) — Critically Endangered category
Gaur or Indian Bison (Bos gaurus) — Vulnerable category
Indian Elephant (Elephas maximus) — Endangered category

questions.explanation: The Gaur (Indian Bison) is listed as Vulnerable by IUCN, a step below Endangered. Bengal Tiger and Indian Elephant are Endangered; Gharial is Critically Endangered. Candidates typically assume all large Indian mammals share the same threat level, making Gaur's lower-threat Vulnerable status a precise recall trap.

questions.stem: The Gangetic River Dolphin (Platanista gangetica), India's National Aquatic Animal, was accorded this status by government notification in which year?

options.option_text: 2005, alongside the National Environment Policy rollout
2009, by a Union Cabinet decision and gazette notification
1997, as part of a Wildlife Protection Act amendment
2012, concurrent with the National Water Policy revision

questions.explanation: The Gangetic River Dolphin was declared India's National Aquatic Animal in 2009 by a Union Cabinet decision. This is frequently tested in IBPS and SSC exams. Option C (1997) targets those who confuse it with a WPA amendment year; Option D (2012) targets those linking it to water-policy reforms.

questions.stem: The legally binding concept of 'Critical Tiger Habitat' (CTH) — designating inviolate core zones within Tiger Reserves — was introduced in India through an amendment to which legislation?

options.option_text: The Forest Rights Act, 2006, which focuses on tribal rights in forests
The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, via the 2006 Amendment Act
The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, under its protected area clauses
The Biological Diversity Act, 2002, under its core-zone provisions

questions.explanation: Section 38V was inserted into the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 by the Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2006, which defined Critical Tiger Habitat as inviolate core zones. The Forest Rights Act (Option A) is a classic distractor — enacted the same year (2006) but concerned with recognising tribal forest rights, not tiger conservation zonation.

questions.stem: Under Section 37 of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, which authority is empowered to notify areas as 'Biodiversity Heritage Sites' in India?

options.option_text: The National Biodiversity Authority acting on a central government directive
The State Government, in consultation with local bodies and institutions
The District Collector, after approval from the State Biodiversity Board
The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change by gazette order

questions.explanation: Section 37 of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 empowers State Governments — not the central government or NBA — to notify Biodiversity Heritage Sites in consultation with local bodies. Option A (NBA) is the strongest distractor because the NBA dominates most BD Act provisions, but site notification is explicitly a state-level function under this section.
